target_objectives: Learner can explain the difference between a classical bit and a qubit
Learner understands superposition as existing in a combination of 0 and 1 until measured

scenes.comment: Hook: Introduce the classical bit as a fundamental binary switch.
scenes.html: Every computer you have ever used speaks in bits. A bit is the simplest possible switch — it is either zero or one. Nothing else.
scenes.speech: Every computer you have ever used speaks in bits. A bit is the simplest possible switch — it is either zero or one. Nothing else.
scenes.tts_narration: [warm, engaging] Every computer you have ever touched speaks in bits. At its core, a bit is the simplest switch imaginable: it is either completely off, or completely on. Zero, or one. Nothing in between.

scenes.comment: Classical bits deep dive: Deterministic behavior, definite states, sequence of flips.
scenes.html: Classical bits are completely deterministic. You always know the exact state. Flip a bit and it moves from zero to one. Flip it again, back to zero. Every bit in your device right now is fixed at exactly one of those two values.
scenes.speech: Classical bits are completely deterministic. You always know the exact state. Flip a bit and it moves from zero to one. Flip it again, back to zero. Every bit in your device right now is fixed at exactly one of those two values.
scenes.tts_narration: [clear, instructive] Classical bits are completely deterministic. When you inspect a bit, its state is never a mystery. Flip the switch, and it moves from zero to one. Flip it again, and it returns to zero. Right now, billions of these tiny switches inside your device are locked into fixed, predictable states.

scenes.comment: Tension beat: Questioning binary limits, opening curiosity.
scenes.html: For decades, all our technology relied on this absolute binary. But what if a switch could be more than just on or off?
scenes.speech: For decades, all our technology relied on this absolute binary. But what if a switch could be more than just on or off?
scenes.tts_narration: [thoughtful, intrigued] For nearly a century, every algorithm and machine we built depended on that rigid rule. [pause] But what if a switch could be something more than just on or off?

scenes.comment: Introduce qubit: Superposition, combinations of 0 and 1, collapse upon measurement.
scenes.html: Meet the qubit. Unlike a classical bit, a qubit can exist in a superposition of zero and one simultaneously. Only when you make a measurement does it collapse to a definite answer.
scenes.speech: Meet the qubit. Unlike a classical bit, a qubit can exist in a superposition of zero and one simultaneously. Only when you make a measurement does it collapse to a definite answer.
scenes.tts_narration: [inspiring, wonder] Meet the qubit. In quantum physics, a qubit does not have to choose zero or one right away. It exists in superposition — a smooth blend of both possibilities at once. It only commits to a single value the moment you perform a measurement.

scenes.comment: Side-by-side comparison: Discrete states vs continuous state sphere.
scenes.html: Side by side, the difference is clear. A classical bit is a single switch with two discrete positions. A qubit is a sphere of possibilities — holding a continuum of states until measured.
scenes.speech: Side by side, the difference is clear. A classical bit is a single switch with two discrete positions. A qubit is a sphere of possibilities — holding a continuum of states until measured.
scenes.tts_narration: [analytical, confident] Side by side, the contrast is unmistakable. A classical bit is a rigid switch, locked to either zero or one. A qubit is a sphere of possibilities — pointing anywhere across a continuous surface until measurement snaps it back to reality.

scenes.comment: Entanglement teaser: Single-sentence hook for correlated qubits.
scenes.html: When two qubits interact, they can become entangled — where measuring one instantly reveals the other across any distance.
scenes.speech: When two qubits interact, they can become entangled — where measuring one instantly reveals the other across any distance.
scenes.tts_narration: [dramatic, hushed] And when two qubits interact, they can become entangled — mysteriously linking their fates so measuring one reveals the other across any distance in the universe.

scenes.comment: Wrap-up and transition into building real quantum circuits.
scenes.html:
FOUNDATION ACQUIRED • BITS VS QUBITS
You now know what separates a bit from a qubit. Next, we will step inside the lab and manipulate our first quantum state.
scenes.speech: You now know what separates a bit from a qubit. Next, we will step inside the lab and manipulate our first quantum state.
scenes.tts_narration: [upbeat, encouraging] You now hold the core foundation separating classical computing from the quantum frontier. Next, let's step into the lab and manipulate our very first qubit.
